---
title: "Norway's 2026 Housing-Deprivation Divide: Construction Slowdown, Material Hardship, and the Well-being Gap"
description: "How a slowing housing market, persistent material deprivation, and income-based gaps in life satisfaction are reshaping Norwegian society."
date: "2026-08-25"
categories: [SSB, housing, inequality, well-being]
---


Norway presents a paradox familiar to wealthy nations: a country consistently ranked among the world's most prosperous yet grappling with growing disparities in housing access, material well-being, and life satisfaction that cleave sharply along income lines. Three datasets from Statistics Norway allow an unusually integrated view of this divide — tracking what gets built, who goes without, and how contentment itself varies by economic circumstance.

## Data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, error = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(PxWebApiData)
library(scales)
library(ggridges)
library(MetBrewer)

df1 <- NULL
tryCatch({
  raw <- ApiData(
    "https://data.ssb.no/api/v0/no/table/06265",
    Region = TRUE,
    BygnType = TRUE,
    Tid = list(filter = "top", values = 40)
  )
  tmp          <- raw[[1]]
  time_col     <- "år"
  value_col    <- "value"
  series_col   <- "bygningstype"
  df1 <- tmp |>
    mutate(
      value    = as.numeric(.data[[value_col]]),
      time_str = .data[[time_col]],
      date     = case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "M") ~ lubridate::ym(sub("M", "-", time_str)),
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "K") ~ lubridate::yq(sub("K", " Q", time_str)),
        nchar(time_str) == 4               ~ lubridate::ymd(paste0(time_str, "-01-01")),
        TRUE ~ NA_Date_
      )
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(date))
}, error = function(e) message("Fetch failed: ", e$message))

if (is.null(df1) || nrow(df1) == 0) { message("No data returned for df1"); df1 <- NULL }

df2 <- NULL
tryCatch({
  raw <- ApiData(
    "https://data.ssb.no/api/v0/no/table/13634",
    Region = TRUE,
    MaterielleGoder = TRUE,
    Tid = list(filter = "top", values = 40)
  )
  tmp          <- raw[[1]]
  time_col     <- "år"
  value_col    <- "value"
  series_col   <- "materielle goder"
  df2 <- tmp |>
    mutate(
      value    = as.numeric(.data[[value_col]]),
      time_str = .data[[time_col]],
      date     = case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "M") ~ lubridate::ym(sub("M", "-", time_str)),
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "K") ~ lubridate::yq(sub("K", " Q", time_str)),
        nchar(time_str) == 4               ~ lubridate::ymd(paste0(time_str, "-01-01")),
        TRUE ~ NA_Date_
      )
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(date))
}, error = function(e) message("Fetch failed: ", e$message))

if (is.null(df2) || nrow(df2) == 0) { message("No data returned for df2"); df2 <- NULL }

df3 <- NULL
tryCatch({
  raw <- ApiData(
    "https://data.ssb.no/api/v0/no/table/13764",
    Tilfredshet = TRUE,
    Inntektsgruppe = TRUE,
    Tid = list(filter = "top", values = 40)
  )
  tmp          <- raw[[1]]
  time_col     <- "år"
  value_col    <- "value"
  series_col   <- "tilfredshet"
  df3 <- tmp |>
    mutate(
      value    = as.numeric(.data[[value_col]]),
      time_str = .data[[time_col]],
      date     = case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "M") ~ lubridate::ym(sub("M", "-", time_str)),
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "K") ~ lubridate::yq(sub("K", " Q", time_str)),
        nchar(time_str) == 4               ~ lubridate::ymd(paste0(time_str, "-01-01")),
        TRUE ~ NA_Date_
      )
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(date))
}, error = function(e) message("Fetch failed: ", e$message))

if (is.null(df3) || nrow(df3) == 0) { message("No data returned for df3"); df3 <- NULL }
```

## Wrangling


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# ── df1: housing starts by building type ──────────────────────────────────────
df1_national   <- NULL
df1_type_total <- NULL
df1_recent     <- NULL

if (!is.null(df1) && nrow(df1) > 0) {
  # Keep national totals (region == "Hele landet" or similar)
  region_col <- if ("region" %in% names(df1)) "region" else
                if ("Region" %in% names(df1)) "Region" else NULL

  if (!is.null(region_col)) {
    national_val <- df1 |>
      pull(.data[[region_col]]) |>
      unique() |>
      (\(x) x[grepl("hele|total|landet|00", x, ignore.case = TRUE)][1])()

    df1_national <- df1 |>
      filter(.data[[region_col]] == national_val,
             .data[["bygningstype"]] %in% c("Enebolig",
                                             "Tomannsbolig",
                                             "Rekkehus, kjedehus og andre småhus",
                                             "Boligblokk")) |>
      group_by(date, bygningstype) |>
      summarise(value = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  } else {
    df1_national <- df1 |>
      filter(.data[["bygningstype"]] %in% c("Enebolig",
                                             "Tomannsbolig",
                                             "Rekkehus, kjedehus og andre småhus",
                                             "Boligblokk")) |>
      group_by(date, bygningstype) |>
      summarise(value = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  }

  if (nrow(df1_national) > 0) {
    df1_type_total <- df1_national |>
      group_by(bygningstype) |>
      summarise(total = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
      arrange(desc(total))

    df1_recent <- df1_national |>
      filter(date >= max(date) - years(10))
  }
}

# ── df2: material deprivation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
df2_national  <- NULL
df2_trend     <- NULL
df2_latest    <- NULL

if (!is.null(df2) && nrow(df2) > 0) {
  region_col2 <- if ("region" %in% names(df2)) "region" else
                 if ("Region" %in% names(df2)) "Region" else NULL

  if (!is.null(region_col2)) {
    national_val2 <- df2 |>
      pull(.data[[region_col2]]) |>
      unique() |>
      (\(x) x[grepl("hele|total|landet|00", x, ignore.case = TRUE)][1])()

    df2_national <- df2 |>
      filter(.data[[region_col2]] == national_val2)
  } else {
    df2_national <- df2
  }

  df2_trend <- df2_national |>
    filter(.data[["materielle goder"]] %in% c(
      "Ikke råd til å holde boligen passe varm",
      "Ikke råd til å spise kjøtt og fisk annenhver dag",
      "Ikke råd til å gå til tannlege",
      "Ikke råd til å bytte ut utslitte møbler",
      "Mangler minst ett materielt gode"
    )) |>
    rename(deprivation = `materielle goder`)

  if (nrow(df2_trend) > 0) {
    df2_latest <- df2_trend |>
      filter(date == max(date))
  }
}

# ── df3: life satisfaction by income group ────────────────────────────────────
df3_clean       <- NULL
df3_livet       <- NULL
df3_all_wide    <- NULL
df3_dumbbell    <- NULL
income_col_name <- NULL

if (!is.null(df3) && nrow(df3) > 0) {
  # Identify income column
  income_col_name <- if ("inntektsgruppe" %in% names(df3)) "inntektsgruppe" else
                     if ("Inntektsgruppe" %in% names(df3)) "Inntektsgruppe" else NULL

  df3_clean <- df3 |>
    filter(.data[["tilfredshet"]] %in% c(
      "Livet alt i alt",
      "Fysisk helse",
      "Psykisk helse",
      "Økonomisk situasjon",
      "Forhold til venner"
    ))

  if (!is.null(income_col_name) && nrow(df3_clean) > 0) {
    # Life satisfaction overall over time by income group
    df3_livet <- df3_clean |>
      filter(.data[["tilfredshet"]] == "Livet alt i alt")

    # Latest year dumbbell: compare lowest vs highest income group
    latest_year <- max(df3_clean$date)

    income_groups <- df3_clean |>
      pull(.data[[income_col_name]]) |>
      unique()

    # Try to identify low and high income groups
    low_group  <- income_groups[grepl("lav|lav|under|1\\.|første|lavest|lowest|low",
                                       income_groups, ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
    high_group <- income_groups[grepl("høy|høy|over|4\\.|fjerde|høyest|highest|high",
                                       income_groups, ignore.case = TRUE)][1]

    if (!is.na(low_group) && !is.na(high_group)) {
      df3_dumbbell <- df3_clean |>
        filter(date == latest_year,
               .data[[income_col_name]] %in% c(low_group, high_group)) |>
        select(tilfredshet, income = .data[[income_col_name]], value) |>
        pivot_wider(names_from = income, values_from = value) |>
        rename(low_val = all_of(low_group), high_val = all_of(high_group)) |>
        # fixed: convert to numeric before subtraction to avoid non-numeric argument error
        mutate(
          low_val = as.numeric(low_val),
          high_val = as.numeric(high_val),
          gap = high_val - low_val
        )
    }

    df3_all_wide <- df3_clean |>
      filter(date == latest_year) |>
      select(tilfredshet, income = .data[[income_col_name]], value)
  }
}
```

## The Construction Picture: What Norway Is Building (and What It Is Not)

Housing supply shapes access for everyone, but particularly for lower-income households who depend on affordable stock. New builds by type reveal whether Norway is expanding the right kinds of housing to meet broad demand.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pal_housing <- met.brewer("Hokusai2", n = 4)

if (exists("df1_recent") && !is.null(df1_recent) && nrow(df1_recent) > 0) {
  p <- ggplot(df1_recent, aes(x = date, y = value, fill = bygningstype)) +
    geom_area(alpha = 0.85, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_housing, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format()) +
    labs(
      title = "Dwelling starts by building type, Norway",
      subtitle = "Number of dwellings started annually, stacked by building type",
      x = NULL, y = "Dwellings started",
      caption = "Source: Statistics Norway, table 06265"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
  print(p)

  total_recent <- df1_recent |>
    group_by(date) |>
    summarise(total = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  peak_year <- total_recent[which.max(total_recent$total), ]
  latest_year_val <- total_recent[which(total_recent$date == max(total_recent$date)), ]
  top_type <- df1_type_total[1, ]

  cat(sprintf(
    "\nAcross the period shown, peak annual dwelling starts reached %s in %s. The most recent year recorded %s starts. The building type accounting for the largest cumulative share of new supply is %s.\n\n",
    comma(peak_year$total),
    format(peak_year$date, "%Y"),
    comma(latest_year_val$total),
    top_type$bygningstype
  ))
} else {
  cat("\n*Figure omitted — Statistics Norway returned no data for this series.*\n\n")
}
```

## Who Goes Without: Material Deprivation in Norway

Even a prosperous society carries pockets of genuine hardship. Statistics Norway measures several dimensions of material deprivation — from the ability to keep a home adequately warm to affording regular dental care. These indicators are arguably more revealing than income statistics alone, because they capture lived experience rather than relative thresholds.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pal_dep <- met.brewer("Redon", n = 5)

if (exists("df2_trend") && !is.null(df2_trend) && nrow(df2_trend) > 0) {

  # Create short labels for facets
  df2_plot <- df2_trend |>
    mutate(
      dep_label = case_when(
        grepl("varm",      deprivation, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Cannot keep\nhome warm",
        grepl("kjøtt",     deprivation, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Cannot afford\nmeat/fish\nevery 2nd day",
        grepl("tannlege",  deprivation, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Cannot afford\ndentist",
        grepl("møbler",    deprivation, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Cannot replace\nworn furniture",
        grepl("minst ett", deprivation, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Lacks at least\none material good",
        TRUE ~ deprivation
      )
    )

  p <- ggplot(df2_plot, aes(x = date, y = value, colour = dep_label, fill = dep_label)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_area(alpha = 0.12) +
    facet_wrap(~ dep_label, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal_dep, guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_dep, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "4 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
    labs(
      title = "Material deprivation indicators, Norway",
      subtitle = "Share of population (%) reporting each form of material hardship, by year",
      x = NULL, y = "Percentage",
      caption = "Source: Statistics Norway, table 13634"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
  print(p)

  latest_dep <- df2_latest |>
    arrange(desc(value))
  top_dep    <- latest_dep[1, ]
  lowest_dep <- latest_dep[nrow(latest_dep), ]

  cat(sprintf(
    "\nIn the most recent year of available data (%s), the most prevalent form of material hardship was '%s', affecting %s%% of the population. The least prevalent was '%s' at %s%%.\n\n",
    format(max(df2_trend$date), "%Y"),
    top_dep$deprivation,
    round(top_dep$value, 1),
    lowest_dep$deprivation,
    round(lowest_dep$value, 1)
  ))
} else {
  cat("\n*Figure omitted — Statistics Norway returned no data for this series.*\n\n")
}
```

## Well-being and the Income Divide

The final thread connects economic circumstance to subjective well-being. Norway's living conditions surveys ask respondents to rate satisfaction across multiple life domains. When these scores are broken down by income group, a consistent pattern emerges — one that quantifies the human cost of economic inequality.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (exists("df3_all_wide") && !is.null(df3_all_wide) && nrow(df3_all_wide) > 0) {

  pal_ridge <- met.brewer("Hokusai2", n = length(unique(df3_all_wide$income)))

  p <- ggplot(df3_all_wide, aes(x = value, y = income, fill = income, colour = income)) +
    geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.65, scale = 1.2, rel_min_height = 0.01,
                        bandwidth = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_ridge, guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal_ridge, guide = "none") +
    labs(
      title = "Distribution of life-satisfaction scores by income group",
      subtitle = "Density of satisfaction scores across domains (latest available year), by income group",
      x = "Satisfaction score", y = NULL,
      caption = "Source: Statistics Norway, table 13764"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
  # fixed: added explicit print() to render the plot
  print(p)

  group_means <- df3_all_wide |>
    group_by(income) |>
    summarise(mean_sat = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(desc(mean_sat))

  top_inc  <- group_means[1, ]
  low_inc  <- group_means[nrow(group_means), ]
  gap_val  <- top_inc$mean_sat - low_inc$mean_sat

  cat(sprintf(
    "\nAcross all satisfaction domains in the latest year, the income group '%s' records the highest mean score (%.1f), while '%s' records the lowest (%.1f) — a gap of %.1f points.\n\n",
    top_inc$income, top_inc$mean_sat,
    low_inc$income, low_inc$mean_sat,
    gap_val
  ))
} else {
  cat("\n*Figure omitted — Statistics Norway returned no data for this series.*\n\n")
}
```

## Key Findings


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
findings <- character(0)

if (exists("df1_recent") && !is.null(df1_recent) && nrow(df1_recent) > 0) {
  total_recent <- df1_recent |>
    group_by(date) |>
    summarise(total = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  peak_row   <- total_recent[which.max(total_recent$total), ]
  latest_row <- total_recent[which(total_recent$date == max(total_recent$date)), ]
  top_type   <- df1_type_total[1, ]
  findings <- c(findings, sprintf(
    "**Housing supply (table 06265):** Dwelling starts peaked at %s in %s. The most recent year recorded %s starts. %s dominates cumulative new supply.",
    comma(peak_row$total), format(peak_row$date, "%Y"),
    comma(latest_row$total), top_type$bygningstype
  ))
}

if (exists("df2_latest") && !is.null(df2_latest) && nrow(df2_latest) > 0) {
  top_dep <- df2_latest |> arrange(desc(value)) |> slice(1)
  findings <- c(findings, sprintf(
    "**Material deprivation (table 13634):** In the most recent year, the most common hardship was '%s', reported by %.1f%% of the population.",
    top_dep$deprivation, top_dep$value
  ))
}

if (exists("df3_all_wide") && !is.null(df3_all_wide) && nrow(df3_all_wide) > 0) {
  group_means <- df3_all_wide |>
    group_by(income) |>
    summarise(mean_sat = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(desc(mean_sat))
  top_inc <- group_means[1, ]
  low_inc <- group_means[nrow(group_means), ]
  gap_val <- top_inc$mean_sat - low_inc$mean_sat
  findings <- c(findings, sprintf(
    "**Life satisfaction (table 13764):** Across all domains, the gap between the highest and lowest income groups averages %.1f satisfaction points, with the highest group ('%s') scoring %.1f and the lowest ('%s') scoring %.1f.",
    gap_val, top_inc$income, top_inc$mean_sat, low_inc$income, low_inc$mean_sat
  ))
}

if (length(findings) > 0) {
  cat("### Summary\n\n")
  for (f in findings) {
    cat("-", f, "\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("*No data were available to generate key findings.*\n\n")
}
```

## Closing Reflection

Housing, deprivation, and well-being are not separate policy files — they are interlocking components of the same social contract. When construction volumes shift away from affordable typologies, fewer lower-income households can access adequate housing, and the material hardships captured by deprivation indicators tend to deepen. The satisfaction data provide the human dimension: how much subjective well-being depends on economic circumstances, and how large the gap between income groups can become even in a Nordic welfare state. Norway's ability to sustain its reputation for social equality will depend, in part, on how seriously these three datasets are read together by those who shape housing, welfare, and redistributive policy.
